Conclusion: Candidate 1 is the only currently rollout-eligible option because its single sign-on is supplied as included. Candidate 2 cannot proceed unless single sign-on availability before rollout is confirmed. Neither candidate can be selected until its complete current-quarter cost is shown to fit the cap.

Candidate 1 — Proceed only if its quote for 20 editors and expected guests, including mandatory fees and billing terms, stays within the cap and manual exports are acceptable until next quarter. Rule it out if export automation is mandatory before rollout or its complete cost exceeds the cap. If cost or guest terms remain unknown, do not roll it out.

Candidate 2 — Consider it only if single sign-on is confirmed for availability before rollout, its complete cost including guest charges fits the cap, and its advertised exports meet the required scope and automation needs. Rule it out if timely single sign-on cannot be confirmed or total cost exceeds the cap. If confirmation is unavailable, preserve the current state and do not roll it out.

Missing decision inputs: the exact cap; expected guest volume and usage; comparable complete quotes; Candidate 2’s single sign-on timing, guest pricing, and export details; Candidate 1’s guest terms; and whether export automation is mandatory before rollout.
